memory_update.text: DSGX is the highest-confidence direct public-market candidate for tariff/customs/origin/sanctions compliance infrastructure because it owns trade-data, customs, denied-party screening, and regulatory workflow assets.
RLGT is a small-cap underfollowed services-side candidate: customs brokerage and global trade management exposure is plausible but requires verification of materiality and margin contribution.
ULS is a large-cap but underfollowed certification-gate candidate for supplier transparency, forced-labor documentation, and product/supplier data validation rather than tariff classification itself.
TRI should remain a reference anchor for ONESOURCE Global Trade, but its relevant exposure may be too diluted inside a large information-services platform for a pure underfollowed lane.

Two highly relevant assets, e2open and Dun & Bradstreet, are no longer standalone US-listed equities as of 2026-06-13; future searches should map their public acquirers or peers rather than include ETWO or DNB as active US-listed candidates.

summary: Layer 1B expansion found a narrow public-market universe for tariff/customs/origin/sanctions compliance infrastructure. The strongest direct public exposure is Descartes Systems, while Thomson Reuters is a large reference anchor. Underfollowed discovery candidates include Radiant Logistics as a small-cap customs brokerage/global trade-management services play and UL Solutions as a testing/certification/supply-chain transparency gate for forced-labor and supplier compliance. Several highly relevant assets are private or no longer US-listed, including e2open and Dun & Bradstreet, creating a coverage gap.
